definitions.explanation: Walking at a speed faster than normal pace, often as a form of exercise.
A gait of a horse between a walk and a canter, in which diagonal pairs of legs move together.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{速歩|そくほ}で{通勤|つうきん}している。
examples.english: I commute by brisk walking every morning.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}のために{一日|いちにち}{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}の{速歩|そくほ}が{推奨|すいしょう}されている。
examples.english: Thirty minutes of brisk walking per day is recommended for health.

examples.japanese: {速歩|そくほ}とゆっくりした{歩行|ほこう}を{交互|こうご}に{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すインターバル{速歩|そくほ}が{注目|ちゅうもく}されている。
examples.english: Interval walking, which alternates between brisk walking and slow walking, is gaining attention.

examples.japanese: {馬|うま}が{速歩|そくほ}で{走|はし}っている。
{乗馬|じょうば}レッスンでは、まず{常歩|なみあし}を{覚|おぼ}えてから{速歩|そくほ}に{進|すす}む。
examples.english: In horseback riding lessons, you first learn the walk before progressing to the trot.

examples.japanese: {速歩|そくほ}のとき、{騎手|きしゅ}は{馬|うま}のリズムに{合|あ}わせて{体|からだ}を{上下|じょうげ}させる。
examples.english: During the trot, the rider moves their body up and down in rhythm with the horse.

notes:
A compound of {速|そく} (fast, speed) and {歩|ほ} (walk, step). Has two main domains of use: exercise/fitness and equestrian.

In the fitness context, {速歩|そくほ} refers to power walking or brisk walking, which has become popular as a moderate-intensity exercise. "Interval {速歩|そくほ}" is a well-known Japanese exercise method developed at Shinshu University.

In equestrian terminology, {速歩|そくほ} is the standard Japanese term for the trot, one of the basic horse gaits.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- インターバル{速歩|そくほ}: interval walking (exercise method)
- {速歩|そくほ}で{歩|ある}く: to walk briskly
- {速歩|そくほ}{訓練|くんれん}: trot training (equestrian)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {早足|はやあし}: fast pace, quick step — everyday word for walking quickly
- ウォーキング: walking (as exercise) — loanword commonly used for fitness walking
- {常歩|なみあし}: walk (horse gait) — slower than a trot
